chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Ziyād al-Qandī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Qaṣīr, who said:
I entered upon Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام and said to him: May I be made your ransom, I have devised a supplication.

He said: “Leave me aside from your devising. When some matter befalls you, then seek refuge with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and perform two rakʿahs, offering them as a gift to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.”
I said: How should I do it? He said: “You perform ghusl and pray two rakʿahs.” And he mentioned the hadith to its end.
Then Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “I guarantee before Allah that you will not depart from your place until your need is fulfilled.”

key_terms.اخْتِرَاعِكَ: your own invention or devising, referring here to a self-composed supplication
key_terms.دُعَاءً: a supplication that the speaker says he had devised
key_terms.فَافْزَعْ: turn urgently for refuge or recourse

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in Shiʿi hadith when a serious need or difficulty befalls him?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that when a pressing need descends upon a person, he should turn to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم through an act of worship rather than relying on self-devised supplications. It describes performing ghusl and praying two rakʿahs as a gift to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and it emphasizes confidence in the fulfillment of one's need through this devotional practice.
